 Judgment
Sri. Kalyan.R., learned counsel for the appellants and Sri.A.N.Krishna Swamy., learned counsel for respondent No.2 have appeared in person.
2. The claimants have assailed the Judgment of the Tribunal in this appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the respective parties have urged several contentions.
Heard, the contentions urged on NC: 2024:KHC:14936 behalf of the respective parties and perused the appeal papers and also the records with utmost care.
4. The point that requires consideration is whether the claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation.
5. The Claimants appeal is one for enhancement of compensation.
The grounds urged in the present appeal is that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager.
It is noticed that the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.21,49,200/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakh Forty Nine Thousand Two Hundred only) towards Loss of dependency.
It is contended that the deceased was working as FDA at ITI College and was earning Rs.14,925/- (Rupees Fourteen Thousand Nine Hundred and Twenty Five only).

The deceased was aged 39 years as on the date of Smt.Narasamma.R vs Sri.Prabhu.D on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192922850/
2 accident.
The Tribunal has taken into consideration the future prospectus at 20% on the ground that the wife of deceased is getting pension.
This is unsustainable in law.

If the widow is getting pension,
the percentage of future prospectus cannot be reduced.
Since, the deceased was aged 39 years and had permanent job, the future prospectus must be taken into consideration at 50%.
The age of the deceased NC: 2024:KHC:14936 was 39 years as on the date of accident, hence the multiplier 15 is to be adopted.

Hence, the amount towards the loss of dependency is as under:
CALCULATION OF LOSS OF DEPENDENCY
Future prospects:
It is taken into consideration at 50% as per chart because the age of deceased is below 40 years and the deceased had permanent job.
Hence, they are entitled to compensation under the head "Loss of consortium".

In view of law laid down by the Apex Court in PRANAY SETHI's case, the interest should be NC:
2024:KHC:14936 considered to the loss of consortium at the rate of 10% per annum for every three years.
This Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.33,000/- (Rupees Thirty Three Thousand only) towards loss of estate and transportation of the dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremonies.

6. Accordingly, this Court re-determines the compensation as under:-
1. Towards loss of 26,86,500 Rs.26,86,500/- dependency 2.

Towards loss of 1,44,000 Rs.1,44,000/- Consortium 3. Loss of estate & 33,000 Rs.33,000/-
transportation of dead body and funeral and obsequies.

Reassessed compensation Rs.28,63,500/-
NC: 2024:KHC:14936 Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the prevailing rate of interest during the relevant time
, this Court deems it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation amount from the date of claim petition till realization.
